title: Duke making drunk sidemen play, especially Ben Webster
summary: Jones thinks Duke embarrassed players rather than firing them, and that Ben Webster wanted to fight him.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: But how about the times -- yeah, that's when what we're talking about, the competitive spirit there, but there were other times he'd bring people down to take solos, down in front, when they were juiced and couldn't play or couldn't stand up.
Oh, he used to do that to Ben Webster quite often.

What do you think that accomplished? Did you ever wonder about that? I always did, because I mean here the man was not at his best because he was so juiced, and it made the band sound bad or even made him look bad. The audience doesn't understand that this is Duke's discipline.
Well, I think that Duke, rather than giving a guy notice, he would make the guy embarass himself.
But do you think that -- that wouldn't keep Ben Webster from taking a drink the next night, would it?
No. What Ben wanted to do was fight Duke. He wanted to do a Joe Louis or something, you know?
